what: A `blaze-maintained` stdout line for harness/v2/dbsp/edits.py (docs/v2/plan/design/dbsp.md section 10 and 12). Under `--message-format=json`, every `blaze check`/`build`/`test`/`run` prints, for each write the daemon made to the database while serving the request (one file write, a batch, a view change) and for each maintainer and each crate it maintained in that write, one line: {"reason": "blaze-maintained", "write": N (0-based index of the write within this request), "maintainer": "nameres"|"impls" (base_db::Maintainer::name), "crate": "<the crate as cargo names its target: the target name, the same string as compiler-artifact target.name>", "work": {"ops": u64, "woken": u64, "rebuilt": u64, "region": u64, "slices": u64, "keys": u64}} with `work` exactly blaze_dbsp::Work (crates/blaze-dbsp, dbsp-engine). A crate the maintainer ran over with all-zero work still gets its line (the harness asserts zeros for crates the edit did not touch). Carry it as a new field of blaze-api Response::Work / Worked (e.g. `maintained: Vec<Maintained>`), printed by blaze-ui api.rs beside `blaze-work`, before it. The daemon side gets the records from base-db (request to dbsp-engine filed with this). edits.py fails every add-impl step loudly until the line exists; it asserts ops == 1 and slices <= 2 for the edited crate, all zeros for every other crate.
